### workspace plan --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan status [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME] | --all | --file PATH | --group GROUP] [--json]
       workspace plan path [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace plan show [--name WORKSPACE]
       workspace plan init [--name WORKSPACE] [--title TITLE] [--from FILE] [--force] [--json]
       workspace plan start [--name WORKSPACE] [--task ID [--pane PANE | --spawn KIND]] [--json]
       workspace plan pause [--name WORKSPACE] [--interrupt] [--json]
       workspace plan delete [--name WORKSPACE] --yes [--json]
       workspace plan task add --title TEXT [--id ID] [--state STATE] [--reason TEXT] [--phase NAME | --after ID] [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace plan task set-state --task ID --state STATE [--reason TEXT] [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace plan task set-title --task ID --title TEXT [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace plan task move --task ID (--after ID | --before ID | --phase NAME) [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

A plan is IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md in the workspace's notes directory: one checklist
line per task under '## Tasks'. workspace counts it, and works out one state from the
plan, the session and the pane that owns the plan.

Subcommands:
  status          Count the plan and report its state
  path            Print where the plan is (or would be)
  show            Print the plan file
  init            Write a new plan, or import an existing document with --from
  start           Set status: active, then launch the workspace or send its agent the plan
  pause           Set status: paused; the agent stops before its next task
  delete          Rename the plan to IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md.deleted-<time>
  task add        Add one task line to the plan
  task set-state  Set one task's state
  task set-title  Change one task's title
  task move       Move one task line
Run `workspace plan VERB --help` for a verb's options. Task states: done, in_progress, skipped, blocked, todo.

A verb that writes (init, start, pause, delete, task) changes the plan or the workspace for real.

        --name NAME                  Workspace to act on instead of the one detected from the current directory
        --project [NAME]             status: every workspace of a project (NAME, or the project of the current workspace)
        --all                        status: every workspace
        --group GROUP                status: every workspace of every repository in a group (group:billing, billing or Billing; see projects group list)
        --file PATH                  status: read any file, with no workspace and a state from the file alone
        --title TITLE                init: the plan's title (default: the workspace task's title); task add: the task's title; task set-title: the new title
        --from FILE                  init: import this document as the plan
        --force                      init: replace a plan that is already there
        --yes                        delete: confirm the delete
        --task ID                    start: send only this task; task set-state, set-title and move: the task (its id, such as T3)
        --id ID                      task add: the new task's id (default: the next number after the plan's last id)
        --state STATE                task add and set-state: done, in_progress, skipped, blocked, todo
        --reason TEXT                task add and set-state: why a task is blocked or skipped
        --phase NAME                 task add: the ### heading to add under; task move: move to the end of this phase
        --after ID                   task add and move: place the task after this task
        --before ID                  task move: place the task before this task
        --if-revision REV            task: refuse with stale_revision unless the plan's revision is REV
        --pane PANE                  start --task: the pane to send it to, a pane id (%19) or window.pane (0.1)
        --spawn KIND                 start --task: start a new agent pane for it (claude, codex, opencode, pi)
        --interrupt                  pause: interrupt the owner panes that are working
        --json                       Print one JSON document (see docs/README.plan.md)
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan status    # the plan of the workspace you are in, e.g. api.worktree-x  working  7/20 (40%)  T9 Add the token store
  workspace plan status --all --json    # every workspace, as one JSON document
  workspace plan path    # where the plan file is, e.g. /src/api/tmp/workspace-notes/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md
  workspace plan init --title "Auth rewrite"    # write a new plan
  workspace plan start    # set it active, then launch the workspace or type the play into its agent pane
  workspace plan start --task T4 --pane %23    # type one task into pane %23
  workspace plan pause --interrupt    # stop after the current task and interrupt the working owner panes
  workspace plan task add --title "Write the docs" --phase Docs    # add a task under the ### Docs heading
  workspace plan task set-state --task T3 --state blocked --reason "needs the dev database"    # block a task
  workspace plan delete --yes    # rename the plan file to IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md.deleted-<time>
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace plan status --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan status [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME] | --all | --file PATH | --group GROUP] [--json]

Count the plan and report its state.

A workspace with no plan is a row, not an error. With no scope flag it is the current workspace's row
(outside any workspace: not_in_workspace). Give at most one of --name, --project, --all, --file and
--group.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --project [NAME]             Every workspace of a project (NAME, or the project of the current workspace)
    --all                        Every workspace
    --group GROUP                Every workspace of every repository in a group (group:billing, billing or Billing; see projects group list)
    --file PATH                  Read any file, with no workspace and a state from the file alone
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan status    # the plan of the workspace you are in: state, counts and the current task
  workspace plan status --name api.worktree-x    # one workspace by name
  workspace plan status --project    # the plans of the main checkout and its worktrees, such as to see which one is stalled
  workspace plan status --all    # every workspace, one line each (no plan reads "no plan")
  workspace plan status --group billing    # every workspace of every repository in the billing group
  workspace plan status --file IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md    # a plan file in the current directory, with no workspace
  workspace plan status --json    # one JSON document, with the revision that --if-revision takes
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace plan path --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan path [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Print where the plan is (or would be).

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan path    # where the plan of the workspace you are in is, whether or not the file exists
  workspace plan path --name api.worktree-x    # the same for one workspace by name
  workspace plan path --json    # adds exists (is the file there?) and notes_dir

### workspace plan show --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan show [--name WORKSPACE]

Print the plan file.

Exits 1 with an error when there is no plan.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan show    # print the plan of the workspace you are in
  workspace plan show --name api.worktree-x    # print the plan of one workspace by name
  workspace plan show --name api.worktree-x | grep '\[!\]'    # list the blocked tasks of that plan
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace plan init --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan init [--name WORKSPACE] [--title TITLE] [--from FILE] [--force] [--json]

Write a new plan, or import an existing document with --from.

Writes the plan file for real. A plan that is already there is an error (exit 1, plan_exists) unless --force replaces it.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --title TITLE                The plan's title (default: the workspace task's title)
    --from FILE                  Import this document as the plan
    --force                      Replace a plan that is already there
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan init    # write a new plan, titled after the workspace's task if it has one, in the notes directory (it makes the directory)
  workspace plan init --title "Auth rewrite"    # write a new plan with your own title
  workspace plan init --from design.md    # import design.md (read from the current directory) as the plan
  workspace plan init --from design.md --force    # replace the plan that is already there with design.md (the old plan is overwritten)
  workspace plan init --name api.worktree-x --json    # write the plan of another workspace; with a plan there and no --force it exits 1 with plan_exists
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace plan start --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan start [--name WORKSPACE] [--task ID [--pane PANE | --spawn KIND]] [--json]

Set status: active, then launch the workspace or send its agent the plan.

Launches the workspace with the implementation-plan play, or sends the main agent pane the play
and "Continue the plan." (a working pane is left alone).

With --task, sends that one task to --pane, a new agent pane (--spawn), the task's owner, or the
main agent pane; the pane is written onto the task line as its owner.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --task ID                    Send only this task (its id, such as T3)
    --pane PANE                  With --task: the pane to send it to, a pane id (%19) or window.pane (0.1)
    --spawn KIND                 With --task: start a new agent pane for it (claude, codex, opencode, pi)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan start    # set the plan active, then launch the workspace or type the play into its main agent pane
  workspace plan start --name api.worktree-x --json    # the same for one workspace by name, with a JSON action document
  workspace plan start --task T4    # type task T4 into the task's owner pane, else the main agent pane, and write the pane onto the task
  workspace plan start --task T4 --pane %23    # type task T4 into pane %23 of the workspace's session
  workspace plan start --task T5 --spawn claude    # split a new pane, start Claude Code in it and type task T5 there
--- stderr
--- end

--- exit 0
--- stdout

### workspace plan pause --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan pause [--name WORKSPACE] [--interrupt] [--json]

Set status: paused; the agent stops before its next task.

Writes status: paused into the plan file for real. --interrupt also presses the agent's interrupt key (Escape for Claude Code and Codex) in each owner pane that works.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --interrupt                  Interrupt the owner panes that are working
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan pause    # set status: paused; the agent stops before its next task and nothing is interrupted
  workspace plan pause --interrupt    # also press the interrupt key in each owner pane that is working
  workspace plan pause --name api.worktree-x --json    # pause one workspace by name, with a JSON action document
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace plan delete --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan delete [--name WORKSPACE] --yes [--json]

Rename the plan to IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md.deleted-<time>.

Needs --yes, and then renames the plan file for real; the session and worktree stay.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --yes                        Confirm the delete
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan delete --yes    # rename the plan of the workspace you are in to IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md.deleted-<time> for real
  workspace plan delete --name api.worktree-x --yes    # the same for one workspace by name
  workspace plan delete --yes --json    # the same, with a JSON action document; with a plan there and no --yes it exits 1 with confirmation_required (no plan: no_plan)
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace plan task add --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan task add --title TEXT [--id ID] [--state STATE] [--reason TEXT] [--phase NAME | --after ID] [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Add one task line to the plan.

Writes one task line into the plan file for real. Blocked and skipped tasks need --reason.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --title TITLE                The new task's title
    --id ID                      The new task's id (default: the next number after the plan's last id)
    --state STATE                The task's state: done, in_progress, skipped, blocked or todo (default: todo)
    --reason TEXT                Why a task is blocked or skipped
    --phase NAME                 The ### heading to add under
    --after ID                   Place the task after this task
    --if-revision REV            Refuse with stale_revision unless the plan's revision is REV
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan task add --title "Write the docs"    # add a to-do task with the next free id to the plan of this workspace
  workspace plan task add --title "Write the docs" --phase Docs    # add it under the ### Docs heading
  workspace plan task add --title "Add the index" --id T7 --after T3    # give it the id T7 and put it after task T3
  workspace plan task add --title "Wait for CI" --state blocked --reason "CI is down"    # add a blocked task; blocked and skipped need --reason
  workspace plan task add --title "Write the docs" --if-revision 41ec0bd7d8c4ac1b1fb22f22d36eba02a1c9aa56022052bfd20e2b3bf8c030a9 --json    # refuse with stale_revision unless the plan is still at that revision (from plan status --json)
--- stderr
--- end
### workspace plan task add --help --json
--- exit 0

### workspace plan task set-state --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan task set-state --task ID --state STATE [--reason TEXT] [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Set one task's state.

Rewrites one task line of the plan file for real. Blocked and skipped tasks need --reason.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --task ID                    The task (its id, such as T3)
    --state STATE                The new state: done, in_progress, skipped, blocked or todo
    --reason TEXT                Why a task is blocked or skipped
    --if-revision REV            Refuse with stale_revision unless the plan's revision is REV
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan task set-state --task T3 --state done    # mark task T3 done in the plan of this workspace
  workspace plan task set-state --task T3 --state in_progress    # mark it in progress
  workspace plan task set-state --task T3 --state blocked --reason "needs the dev database"    # block it; blocked and skipped need --reason
  workspace plan task set-state --task T3 --state done --if-revision 41ec0bd7d8c4ac1b1fb22f22d36eba02a1c9aa56022052bfd20e2b3bf8c030a9 --json    # refuse with stale_revision unless the plan is still at that revision (from plan status --json)
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace plan task move --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace plan task move --task ID (--after ID | --before ID | --phase NAME) [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Move one task line.

Moves it after or before another task, or to the end of a phase, in the plan file for real.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --task ID                    The task (its id, such as T3)
    --after ID                   Place the task after this task
    --before ID                  Place the task before this task
    --phase NAME                 Move to the end of this phase
    --if-revision REV            Refuse with stale_revision unless the plan's revision is REV
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan task move --task T5 --after T1    # move task T5 to just after task T1
  workspace plan task move --task T5 --before T2    # move task T5 to just before task T2
  workspace plan task move --task T5 --phase Docs    # move task T5 to the end of the ### Docs phase
  workspace plan task move --task T5 --after T1 --if-revision 41ec0bd7d8c4ac1b1fb22f22d36eba02a1c9aa56022052bfd20e2b3bf8c030a9 --json    # refuse with stale_revision unless the plan is still at that revision (from plan status --json)
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace plan
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
Missing subcommand: one of status, path, show, init, start, pause, delete, task.

Usage: workspace plan status [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME] | --all | --file PATH | --group GROUP] [--json]
       workspace plan path [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace plan show [--name WORKSPACE]
       workspace plan init [--name WORKSPACE] [--title TITLE] [--from FILE] [--force] [--json]
       workspace plan start [--name WORKSPACE] [--task ID [--pane PANE | --spawn KIND]] [--json]
       workspace plan pause [--name WORKSPACE] [--interrupt] [--json]
       workspace plan delete [--name WORKSPACE] --yes [--json]
       workspace plan task add --title TEXT [--id ID] [--state STATE] [--reason TEXT] [--phase NAME | --after ID] [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace plan task set-state --task ID --state STATE [--reason TEXT] [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace plan task set-title --task ID --title TEXT [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace plan task move --task ID (--after ID | --before ID | --phase NAME) [--if-revision REV] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

A plan is IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md in the workspace's notes directory: one checklist
line per task under '## Tasks'. workspace counts it, and works out one state from the
plan, the session and the pane that owns the plan.

Subcommands:
  status          Count the plan and report its state
  path            Print where the plan is (or would be)
  show            Print the plan file
  init            Write a new plan, or import an existing document with --from
  start           Set status: active, then launch the workspace or send its agent the plan
  pause           Set status: paused; the agent stops before its next task
  delete          Rename the plan to IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md.deleted-<time>
  task add        Add one task line to the plan
  task set-state  Set one task's state
  task set-title  Change one task's title
  task move       Move one task line
Run `workspace plan VERB --help` for a verb's options. Task states: done, in_progress, skipped, blocked, todo.

A verb that writes (init, start, pause, delete, task) changes the plan or the workspace for real.

        --name NAME                  Workspace to act on instead of the one detected from the current directory
        --project [NAME]             status: every workspace of a project (NAME, or the project of the current workspace)
        --all                        status: every workspace
        --group GROUP                status: every workspace of every repository in a group (group:billing, billing or Billing; see projects group list)
        --file PATH                  status: read any file, with no workspace and a state from the file alone
        --title TITLE                init: the plan's title (default: the workspace task's title); task add: the task's title; task set-title: the new title
        --from FILE                  init: import this document as the plan
        --force                      init: replace a plan that is already there
        --yes                        delete: confirm the delete
        --task ID                    start: send only this task; task set-state, set-title and move: the task (its id, such as T3)
        --id ID                      task add: the new task's id (default: the next number after the plan's last id)
        --state STATE                task add and set-state: done, in_progress, skipped, blocked, todo
        --reason TEXT                task add and set-state: why a task is blocked or skipped
        --phase NAME                 task add: the ### heading to add under; task move: move to the end of this phase
        --after ID                   task add and move: place the task after this task
        --before ID                  task move: place the task before this task
        --if-revision REV            task: refuse with stale_revision unless the plan's revision is REV
        --pane PANE                  start --task: the pane to send it to, a pane id (%19) or window.pane (0.1)
        --spawn KIND                 start --task: start a new agent pane for it (claude, codex, opencode, pi)
        --interrupt                  pause: interrupt the owner panes that are working
        --json                       Print one JSON document (see docs/README.plan.md)
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace plan status    # the plan of the workspace you are in, e.g. api.worktree-x  working  7/20 (40%)  T9 Add the token store
  workspace plan status --all --json    # every workspace, as one JSON document
  workspace plan path    # where the plan file is, e.g. /src/api/tmp/workspace-notes/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md
  workspace plan init --title "Auth rewrite"    # write a new plan
  workspace plan start    # set it active, then launch the workspace or type the play into its agent pane
  workspace plan start --task T4 --pane %23    # type one task into pane %23
  workspace plan pause --interrupt    # stop after the current task and interrupt the working owner panes
  workspace plan task add --title "Write the docs" --phase Docs    # add a task under the ### Docs heading
  workspace plan task set-state --task T3 --state blocked --reason "needs the dev database"    # block a task
  workspace plan delete --yes    # rename the plan file to IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md.deleted-<time>
--- end
